newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore seeks approval for interim budget.
newsitem.headline: Singapore seeks approval for interim budget.

text.p: Singapore's parliament on Monday was asked to approve government expenditure of Singapore $11.4 billion (US$8.14 billion) to cover the first five months of its next fiscal year.

Finance Minister Richard Hu said the vote would ensure government operations continued without disruption in case the budget for the next financial year -- April 1, 1997 to March 31, 1998 -- was delayed.

The budget could be delayed if Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong decided to wait until the last moment before calling a general election in the city state. Under Singapore law, elections can be held at any time up to April 5, 1997.

"But members of parliament should not see this as a signal that elections would be held later and not earlier," Hu said. "This move gives the Prime Minister flexibility if he decides to hold elections later."
Hu said the the present parliament would be dissolved by January 5, 1997.
